market_specific_notes: USCIS states it directly: “We consider all military physicians designated civil surgeons to perform immigration medical examinations at military treatment facilities in the United States for U.S. veterans, members of the U.S. military, and designated dependents.” In San Diego that is a live option rather than a footnote.

Separately, USCIS recognises all state and local health departments as civil surgeons for the refugee vaccination assessment. Locally that points at the County of San Diego Health & Human Services Agency, for that category and for vaccinations only.
Everyone else uses a designated civil surgeon confirmed through the federal locator. Three routes, and the one that applies to you is decided by category, not by convenience.
Before working the checklist below, establish which of the three routes is yours. A veteran or service member who compares civilian prices first may be shopping in the wrong market entirely.
local_vetting_points: If you are a veteran, a service member or a designated dependent, ask the military treatment facility first — before comparing civilian prices.
Otherwise search uscis.gov/tools/find-a-civil-surgeon by ZIP and verify designation there.
Confirm the office's locator listing matches its trading name.
Ask how the practice handles a positive tuberculosis test.
Ask what happens when a vaccination record cannot be found.
typical_cost_ranges: The exam price is not published anywhere. USCIS: “Fees for immigration medical examinations are established by the civil surgeon. Fees may vary by civil surgeon.”
USCIS advises ringing several offices and warns the cost “can vary significantly”.
Ask each office to itemise: examination, tuberculosis and syphilis testing, missing vaccines, completing and sealing the form, follow-up visit.

Filing Form I-693 costs $0. The I-485 filing fee is the published number: paper $1,440 or online $1,390 for an applicant over 14, and paper $950 or online $900 for a child under 14 filing with a parent.
payment_options: USCIS tells applicants to confirm acceptable payment methods with the office before the visit.
Bring the insurance card and ask the narrow question — is this plan accepted for immigration medical examinations? Many plans do not cover all portions.
wait_time_notes: Ask about two timelines, not one: how soon you can be seen, and how soon the form is signed and ready.
Laboratory turnaround and a second visit for vaccines are the usual reasons the second timeline slips.
availability_notes: Ask whether a same-week slot means the examination or the finished paperwork.
If you are close to a filing deadline, put the date to the office and ask for a straight answer.
named_resources_or_providers: USCIS Find a Civil Surgeon locator (official) — uscis.gov/tools/find-a-civil-surgeon
County of San Diego Health & Human Services Agency — sandiegocounty.gov/hhsa. USCIS recognises local health departments as civil surgeons for the refugee vaccination assessment.
Military treatment facilities, for veterans, service members and designated dependents, under the USCIS designation of military physicians as civil surgeons.
USCIS Form I-693 page — uscis.gov/i-693, for the current form edition and filing instructions.
Listings are neutral examples and starting points for your own verification. Nothing here is a ranking or an endorsement.
city_intro_override: San Diego is one of the few markets where the standard advice may not apply to you. USCIS designates military physicians as civil surgeons at military treatment facilities for veterans, service members and designated dependents. If that is your household, check that route before you search the public locator.

primary_city_decision_block.title: Local civil surgeon comparison checklist
items: Veteran, service member or designated dependent? Ask the military treatment facility before anything else.
Refugee adjusting status? The county health agency can complete the vaccination assessment.
Otherwise, verify a civil surgeon through uscis.gov/tools/find-a-civil-surgeon by ZIP.
Ask for the price in five separate lines before comparing offices.
Bring the vaccination records USCIS names.
Confirm the form edition, the signing date, and whether the I-485 goes by mail or online.

heading: San Diego: the military treatment facility route, and everyone else
i693_document_requirements: Form I-693 in the current accepted edition.

Government photo identification such as a valid passport or driver's licence; for applicants aged 14 or younger, identification showing name, date and place of birth and a parent's full name, such as a birth certificate with an English translation, or an affidavit.

A record of vaccinations or immunisations covering what USCIS names: DT, DTP, DTaP, Td, Tdap, OPV, IPV, MMR, Hib, Hepatitis A, Hepatitis B, Varicella, Pneumococcal, Influenza, Rotavirus and Meningococcal disease.
Your health insurance card and payment in an accepted form.
vaccination_handling_notes: Records first. Everything else on this page is cheaper and faster if you arrive with them.
California residents can request their own immunisation record through the state registry; confirm with the clinic which format it will accept.
Refugees adjusting status may complete the vaccination assessment at a state or local health department under the blanket designation.
bilingual_support: The federal locator filters by Languages Spoken across a long named list, and also by doctor's sex. Both come from the practice's own declaration to USCIS.
A language listed in the tool means it exists in the practice. Ask whether it covers the form review specifically.
appointment_booking_notes: Decide the filing method before the exam. Mail: the envelope stays sealed. Online: USCIS instructs you to open it and upload the form, keeping the original and envelope until the case is decided.
Confirm the form edition and signing date — only the 01/20/25 edition is accepted for signatures on or after 3 July 2025.
Ask whether the appointment includes the paperwork or only the examination.

Ask when the sealed packet is released and how a correction is handled if a date or signature is wrong. If you are going through a military treatment facility, ask the same two questions there — the process is not identical.
